s1.syndrome_frame: Facial asymmetry with possible cranial nerve involvement in a neonate
salient_findings: Enhancing mass in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal on MRI
Profound hearing loss in the left ear on auditory brainstem response testing
key_facts: 4-week-old male patient
Left facial asymmetry observed during crying
Passed infant hearing screening previously
MRI showed an enhancing mass in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal
Follow-up MRI showed considerable growth of the mass
Auditory brainstem response testing demonstrated profound hearing loss in the left ear
Histopathological examination revealed a vascular lesion with low levels of mitotic activity
Biphasic lesion composed of vascular nodules among spindle cells
Glomeruloid-like architecture of vascular epithelial nodules
Ki-67 labeling index: 5% to 10%
CD34 and CD31 positive for endothelial cells

shortlist.label: Hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: MRI showed an enhancing mass, histopathological examination revealed a vascular lesion with low levels of mitotic activity

shortlist.label: Lymphangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Glomeruloid-like architecture of vascular epithelial nodules, pattern similar to lymphangiomatosis

shortlist.label: Lymphangiomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological examination revealed a pattern similar to lymphangiomatosis

shortlist.label: Cranial nerve schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mass in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal, profound hearing loss in the left ear

shortlist.label: Vestibular schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mass in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal, profound hearing loss in the left ear

raw.rationale: The histopathological examination revealed a vascular lesion with low levels of mitotic activity, biphasic lesion composed of vascular nodules among spindle cells, and glomeruloid-like architecture of vascular epithelial nodules, which are characteristic features of hemangioma. Additionally, the positive staining for CD34 and CD31, which are endothelial cell markers, further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Lymphangioma
rejected.why: Although the pattern is similar to lymphangiomatosis, the presence of vascular nodules and endothelial cell markers suggests a hemangioma rather than a lymphangioma.

rejected.label: Lymphangiomatosis
rejected.why: The histopathological features, such as the presence of vascular nodules and endothelial cell markers, are not typical of lymphangiomatosis.

rejected.label: Cranial nerve schwannoma
rejected.why: The histopathological examination did not reveal features typical of schwannoma, such as Antoni A and Antoni B areas, and the staining pattern was not consistent with a schwannoma.

rejected.label: Vestibular schwannoma
rejected.why: The location of the mass in the cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal could suggest a vestibular schwannoma, but the histopathological features are not consistent with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Hemangioma is the most likely diagnosis based on the provided information
rejected.why: The combination of clinical presentation, imaging findings, and histopathological features makes hemangioma the most likely diagnosis.
